instantiated_cells.justification: The statute requires expense statements to be filed by principals semiannually (covering 6-month reporting periods), and does not require lobbyists to file annual spending reports.
Only principals file expense statements on July 31 and January 31 for each 6-month reporting period; no monthly lobbyist spending report is required.
The periodic expense reporting obligation is imposed on principals on a semiannual schedule, not on lobbyists under an alternative cadence.
Wisconsin requires principal expense statements twice yearly, not quarterly lobbyist spending reports.
Section 13.68 requires every registered principal (not the lobbyist) to file the periodic expense statement, so there is no separate lobbyist-filed semiannual spending report.
The only periodic expense statement cadence specified is semiannual (6-month reporting periods), not tri-annual tied to the legislative calendar.
Expense itemization requirements in §13.68 apply to the principal’s expense statement; the statute does not require lobbyists to file their own itemized spending reports.
The duty to report legislative proposals/topics is imposed on principals as a condition of authorizing lobbying, not on lobbyists filing a separate activity/spending report.

Compensation to lobbyists is reported in the principal’s expense statement and via lobbyist-provided information to the principal, but the statute does not require lobbyists themselves to disclose their earnings in a lobbyist-filed spending report.
The statute requires principals to keep a daily itemization of time spent meeting/researching, but it does not require lobbyists to disclose contacts in a lobbyist-filed periodic report.
Issue/time allocation reporting is required of principals for topics accounting for 10% or more of time, not an expenditure-per-issue disclosure by lobbyists in their own reports.
Reporting of topics/legislative proposals is imposed on principals (as a prerequisite for lobbying), not on lobbyists through a separate lobbyist spending report.
General subject/topic reporting is required of principals under §13.67(1), not lobbyists as the named filer of a periodic disclosure report.
The periodic disclosure report is filed by the principal under §13.68, so any reporting of gifts/transportation/lodging as 'other costs' is not a lobbyist-filed requirement.
Indirect lobbying costs (e.g., advertising, research) are included in the principal’s expense statement, but lobbyists are not required to file their own indirect-cost spending report.
Wisconsin’s periodic spending disclosure obligation is on registered principals, not lobbyists, so lobbyists are not required to file itemized spending reports with compensation and bill numbers.

While lobbyist license applications may include the address of the applicant’s primary residence, there is no requirement for lobbyists to disclose address/phone in a lobbyist-filed periodic spending report.
The requirement to identify legislative proposals/topics applies to principals and does not create a lobbyist-filed activity/spending report tier.
Disclosure of the principal’s business activity/nature and purposes is required in the principal’s registration statement, not as a lobbyist-filed periodic spending report obligation.

The principal registration statement must list the principal’s business address, but the statute does not require lobbyists to disclose principals’ address/phone in a lobbyist-filed periodic spending report.

Although authorizations identify which principal a lobbyist represents and lobbyists provide information for the principal’s report, there is no requirement that lobbyists file a periodic report listing all principals represented.
Bill/proposal reporting is done by the principal under §13.67(1), not by lobbyists in a lobbyist-filed periodic spending report.
Direct lobbying costs such as compensation are required to be included in the principal’s expense statement, not disclosed by lobbyists as the named filer of a separate spending report.
Total lobbying expenditures are reported by the principal in its expense statement, and the statute does not require lobbyists to file a separate report of total expenditures.
Because the statute assigns periodic itemized spending disclosure to principals rather than lobbyists, the lobbyist-report requirement described in the scoring prompt does not exist.
The statute mandates periodic expense statements by principals, not by lobbyists, so it does not impose a 'no spending/no activity' report requirement on lobbyists.
No provision requires lobbyists to report spending on household members of public officials in a lobbyist-filed spending report; periodic spending reports are filed by principals.
Itemization requirements in §13.68 apply to principals’ filings and do not establish that lobbyists must disclose itemized expenditures in a lobbyist-filed periodic report.
